newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end Tokyo higher ahead of 10-yr JGB auction.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end Tokyo higher ahead of 10-yr JGB auction.

text.p: Key 10-year yen bond futures ended higher on Wednesday as cash bond buying continued from Tuesday, with investors defying expectations they would be sidelined ahead of Thursday's scheduled auction of new 10-year JGBs.

The key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended up 0.69 at 124.80 in turnover of 43,872 contracts. The contract jumped, especially after its break above a chart resistance point of 124.67 just before the close, traders said.
"Dealers realised during Tuesday's session that investors are willing to buy 2.7 percent 10-year JGBs, and that was the decisive factor," said a dealer at a major securities house.
Investors usually refrain from buying bonds before an auction, in order to keep the coupon rate of the new bonds from falling. But this time was different, traders said.
A variety of investors, including public funds, bought recently issued 10-year JGBs on Tuesday, and this was followed by medium- to long-term bond buying on Wednesday, they said.

The yield of the 191st 2.8 percent 10-year JGBs issued in December fell to 2.705 percent from Tuesday's 2.770. This yield will be a key factor when the Ministry of Finance sets the coupon of the 10-year JGBs to be auctioned Thursday and issued later this month.
Traders said the 10-year JGB auction may not damage the market even though a record-low 2.7 percent coupon is likely.

"The recent recovery from the year-end correction encouraged us to believe that investor buying will always emerge on dips," said a dealer at the securities unit of a long-term credit bank. "The current sentiment would not be hurt by tomorrow's auction even with a coupon rate likely to be set at 2.7 percent."
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGBs closed at 2.505 percent, down from Tuesday's 2.570 percent.
Also supportive for the JGB market were a tumble in Tokyo stocks and the yen's strength against the dollar.

"Apart from cash bond buying, lower stocks and the strong yen both yesterday and today were also favourable for bonds," said a long-term credit bank dealer. "But it seems it will be difficult for the key March JGB futures to rise past 125.00, as profit taking awaits above that level," he said.

Earlier this morning, expectations of outright bond buying by the Bank of Japan (BOJ) also helped underpin prices, traders said. As was expected, the BOJ offered to buy 100 billion yen worth of bonds outright at its 0110 GMT operation.

The BOJ surprised the market in late December by cutting the amount of outright bond purchases to 100 billion yen from the usual 200 billion yen. The move triggered a sharp correction in JGBs late last year.
But traders said a consensus had formed that the BOJ in today's operation would buy 100 billion yen worth of bonds. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk (81-33432-8570)
